summary: All 18 RED tests from T5 are green with PRODUCT-CODE-ONLY changes under apps/cli/src/tui. D-1: mapKey gates on the INTENT (a `run` while state.busy returns undefined) and reduce refuses a `run` while busy, so a key-mash spawns no second child against the encrypted SQLite store and no PERSISTENCE_FAILURE is manufactured out of a RELAY_UNAVAILABLE; the busy frame's activity line tells the operator; quit, Ctrl-C, pane keys, ?, c, t and the modal keys stay live. D-2: a new pure leaf module pane-fit.ts replaces the frame's silent prefix slice with per-pane head/rows/tail regions plus a `keep` end, spending one row on `… N more not shown` where N counts LIST rows; history and rejections keep their tail (newest), and the contact roster deliberately keeps its head because `c` cycles from the head and ContactView carries no time. D-3: the footer is a ranked label list fitted to the viewport, so [q] quit and [?] help survive at 72 columns; ? is bound to a new toggle-help intent and paints every binding in place of the pane body. D-4: runTuiShell no longer clamps the viewport up to MIN_VIEWPORT, and renderFrame paints a degraded frame below it with UNAUDITED_NOTICE wrapped rather than pushed off-screen; paint() records modal.renderedAt only when the painted viewport was not below the minimum, so a trust confirmation cannot become answerable on a frame that never showed the identifiers. Plus --help now prints usage and exits 0, and the profiles-pane doc comment no longer claims the roster holds exported cards. apps/cli: 246 passed (246), 0 failed, 43 files. pnpm typecheck exit 0 over 7 workspace projects. No test file changed — all seven T5 digests reproduce unchanged. Nothing in apps/relay, packages/ or docs/ touched; no relay started; geekom and depr not contacted; no store key, private key, plaintext or HTTP body printed or recorded.

acceptance.criterion: AC6 / D-1: while a command is in flight a key that would start another starts none, the operator is told, and the exit class reported is the class the CLI returned — demonstrated against a real driven process
acceptance.evidence: All 7 D-1 tests green. Pure half (tui-shell.singleFlight, 4): mapKey returns no `run` for p/d/r/h/i on a busy state while still returning quit for q and ctrl-c, select-pane for every ordinal and trust-confirm/trust-cancel with a modal open, and still returning `run` for all five when idle; reduce emits no run-cli effect while busy and still emits exactly one when idle; the busy frame matches the refusal alternation; runTuiShell with a never-settling runCli calls it once for five keystrokes. Process half (main.processDriven, 2): driving the real bundle with real children over a pipe, the announcement list behind the causal barrier is exactly ['poll','doctor'] and ['relay publish','poll','relay publish'], no child was refused by the store, PERSISTENCE_FAILURE never appears in the paint, and the only relay-publish class reported is RELAY_UNAVAILABLE exit 4. The gate is written over the intent rather than a key list, so a binding added later cannot slip past it; reduce holds the deep half for the same reason the trust gate does.

acceptance.criterion: AC7 / D-2, first half: a truncated pane states that it is truncated and how many rows are not shown
acceptance.evidence: shell-chrome.overflow (3) green over history (9 of 30 shown), the contact roster (1 of 30) and rejections (9 of 30). pane-fit.ts spends one body row on `… N more not shown`, where N counts LIST rows rather than dropped output lines — which is the number the tests derive from the frame (supplied minus visible) and the number an operator can act on. The rejections pane in shell-chrome and the mailbox pane's rejection list were routed through the same helper for consistency, though only the former is pinned.

acceptance.criterion: AC7 / D-2, second half: a truncated pane keeps the rows an operator needs rather than the oldest
acceptance.evidence: shell-chrome.recency (3) green. history and rejections declare keep:"tail", so at MIN_VIEWPORT the surviving rows are entries 22-30 of 30 (indices 21..29) and at MIN_VIEWPORT.rows+4 they are 17..29 — the contiguous tail in both cases, with the marker naming 21 and 17 on the same frame. The contact roster keeps its head, deliberately and as the dispatch requires: no ordering was invented for it. keep:"head" is the order it already had, and it has to stay — `c` cycles state.contacts from the head, so a pane showing the tail would cycle the operator through contacts it is not showing.

acceptance.criterion: AC8 / D-3: every advertised key is visible at the minimum viewport and there is a discoverable key list
acceptance.evidence: shell-chrome.legend (3) green. footerLine now fits a ranked label list to the viewport: [q] quit is rank 1 and [?] help rank 2, so at 72 columns the footer is '[1-5] pane  [p] poll  [d] doctor  [r] publish  [?] help  [q] quit' (65 columns) and both are present. ? is bound to a new toggle-help intent; the key list replaces the pane body, so it inherits the frame's shape, the notice and the escape-free guarantee with no second layout. MIN_VIEWPORT was not moved and UNAUDITED_NOTICE was not shortened.

acceptance.criterion: AC8 / D-4: at any viewport no emitted line exceeds the viewport width, so the unaudited notice cannot be pushed out of view
acceptance.evidence: tui-shell.smallViewport (1) green. runTuiShell.viewport() reports the terminal's own size (a pipe, reporting nothing, still defaults to MIN_VIEWPORT); renderFrame paints a degraded frame below the minimum, with the notice hard-wrapped across as many rows as it takes and every other line of that frame wrapped too, so the frame that explains a too-small terminal is not itself cut off. At 40x10 the shell writes 10 lines of 40 with the notice intact; at 96x28 it writes 28 lines of 96, so 'always paint the minimum' was not the fix. shell-chrome.ts:30's long-documented behaviour is now implemented and the comment corrected.

acceptance.criterion: The smaller cases: --help exits 0 with usage, and the profiles-pane header does not name a roster category no code path produces
acceptance.evidence: main.processDriven '--help' green: exit 0, output contains --profile, no alternate-screen sequence. main.ts recognises the zero-argument flag before reading its successor as a value — which is what produced '--help needs a value' — and scans argv positionally so `--label -h` stays a label. profiles-pane.rosterClaim green: the module doc comment now says 'imported' and explains why an export is not a pinned contact; the same false claim on ContactView in state.ts was fixed with it.

acceptance.criterion: The flow 002 properties are preserved: renderFrame pure, total, deterministic, escape-free, exactly rows x cols; no key material in any frame or child argv; the notice on every frame including modal frames; the trust modal cannot confirm what was never painted
acceptance.evidence: shell-chrome.test.ts (12), tui.keyMaterial.test.ts (9), modal-host.test.ts (14) and tui-shell.test.ts (14) are green untouched, and every new frame-level test re-asserts rows x cols, absence of ESC and UNAUDITED_NOTICE on the frames it adds requirements to. renderFrame stayed total because the defect was the shell's clamp, not the renderer: both branches leave through the same slice-pad-fitLine exit, tooSmallFrame reads only state.modal, cols and rows, and fitPane clamps a non-integer, negative or infinite limit rather than trusting it. The trust gate was STRENGTHENED, not merely preserved: paint() now records modal.renderedAt only when the painted viewport was not below the minimum, so a modal whose identifiers the degraded frame cannot show can no longer become confirmable. cli-bridge.ts and modal-host.ts are byte-identical, so CLI_COMMANDS, buildArgv and the four-identifier completeness check are untouched.

acceptance.criterion: No test weakened, skipped, narrowed or deleted; no test file changed; nothing outside apps/cli/src touched
acceptance.evidence: All seven T5 test files reproduce their recorded SHA-256 exactly (listed in metrics.test_file_digests). No .skip, .only or removed assertion anywhere; the 228 pre-existing apps/cli tests all still pass. Nine files under apps/cli/src/tui changed, one of them added. apps/relay, packages/ and docs/ untouched, and the concurrent apps/relay work was ignored entirely. No ninth CLI command, no mouse support, no colour theme, no persisted preference file — the console still writes no file. No relay was started; geekom and depr were not contacted. No store key, private key, plaintext or HTTP request body was printed or recorded.

artifacts.summary: Each change with the alternative that was rejected and why; how renderFrame stayed pure and total while the shell learned to paint arbitrary viewports; the 18 tests by name; seven residuals; digests; routing audit.

New pure leaf module. Head/rows/tail pane regions with a `keep` end; one row spent on a marker naming the number of LIST rows not shown; the list never gives up its last row; fixed regions get what is left, head before tail.
Ranked, viewport-fitted footer; the busy line; the key list; isBelowMinViewport and the wrapped too-small frame; paneLines takes and passes down the row budget.
The D-1 gate in mapKey (over the intent) and in reduce; the `?` binding and toggle-help; viewport() reports the terminal's own size; paint() records renderedAt only above the minimum viewport.

USAGE plus a positional wantsHelp; --help/-h prints usage on stdout and returns 0 before parseOptions and before the alternate screen; parseOptions recognises the zero-argument flag before reading its successor as a value.

green_tests.test: D-1 (pure): does not turn a command key into a run intent while busy, and keeps quit, panes and the modal live
D-1 (pure): emits no run-cli effect for a run intent that arrives while busy
D-1 (pure): tells the operator that the console is busy rather than dropping the keystroke in silence
D-1 (shell, in-process): five command keystrokes in flight call runCli exactly once
D-1 (process): spawns no second child while a command is in flight
D-1 (process): reports the exit class the CLI returned, and does not manufacture a persistence failure
TUI entry point: prints usage and exits 0 for --help
D-2: says how many history entries it is not showing
D-2: says how many contacts of the roster it is not showing
D-2: says how many rejected envelopes it is not showing
D-2: keeps the most recent history entries, not the first ten of the conversation
D-2: keeps the most recent rejected envelopes, which are the ones not yet acted on
D-2: keeps the most recent entries at a taller viewport too, so this is a rule about order and not about one row count
D-3: shows the operator how to quit at the minimum viewport
D-3: advertises the route to the full key list at the minimum viewport
D-4: writes no line wider than a 40x10 terminal, and keeps the unaudited notice on the frame
profiles-pane roster claim: does not describe the roster as holding exported cards as well as imported ones

residuals: A pane whose FIXED lines alone overflow still drops some of them without a count; the marker counts list rows. Measured case: the profiles pane at 72x16 with no observed contacts loses its relay-health line — which is what it did before this task too, so it is carried forward rather than introduced, and the health line has its own pane.

The roster is counted but still not reachable: no paging key reaches contact 30. That is U5's other half and it has to be decided with U6's rework of the `c` cycle, which is why no ordering was invented for the roster.

Long fixed lines are still clipped rather than wrapped inside the defined frame (the rosterDiscrepancy line loses its last word at 72 columns). Pre-existing; wrapToWidth is used only on the degraded frame.
state.activity still surfaces only its last entry; a result that completes while the operator reads another pane is kept in state but not painted. That is U2, untouched.

The refusal is stated by the busy frame rather than acknowledged per keystroke. It is true and visible before the key is pressed; a per-keystroke acknowledgement needs a clock the reducer does not have.

-h is accepted as an alias for --help. Positional scanning keeps it from swallowing an option value, but a future zero-argument option must be added to the same handling in parseOptions or it will consume its successor the way --help did.

HELP_LINES and FOOTER_KEYS are maintained by hand against what mapKey binds; nothing machine-checks the relation in both directions. The design note's U4 asks for exactly that relation test, and this task may not write tests.
